The '''2019–20 season''' was [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s 118th season of competitive [[Association football|football]], 91st season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]] and 23rd season in the [[Premier League]]. In addition to the [[2019–20 Premier League|league]], the club competed in the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]], as holders of both competitions. They also entered the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], hoping to win the team's first European trophy since [[1970 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|1970]]. At the start of the season, City defeated [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to win their second consecutive and sixth overall [[2019 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]]. The Citizens also successfully retained the [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], making it their third consecutive League Cup win and their fifth in seven seasons.

The season covered the period from 1 July 2019 to 31 August 2020, having been extended from 30 June 2020 for an indefinite period following the suspension of all elite sport in the UK in March 2020 as part of the response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The domestic season resumed on 17 June, and concluded on 26 July, while the Champions League resumed on 7 August.

This was the first season since [[2007–08 Manchester City F.C. season|2007–08]] without former captain [[Vincent Kompany]], who departed to [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]].

==Season review==
Manchester City began the season as unprecedented holders of all four domestic competitions. Their first successful defence came on 4 August, as they defeated [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on penalties at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] in the [[2019 FA Community Shield]], the traditional curtain raiser to the season.

Acknowledging that City would be judged by their [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] performance after all,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51344995|title=Pep Guardiola: I'll be judged a failure at Man City without Champions League win|website=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2020|access-date=23 August 2020}}</ref> Pep Guardiola said that the new season's main objective would be to win the European title. The Cityzens progressed to the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]] as comfortable group winners and faced old foes [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] there. City won the away game 2–1, but the remainder of the tournament was indefinitely postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe|COVID-19 pandemic]]. Eventually, [[UEFA]] announced that the tournament would be resumed in August 2020 [[Behind closed doors (sport)#COVID-19 pandemic|behind closed doors]]. After eight domestic trophies were clinched with Guardiola, fans eagerly await the team's first European title since 1970. The home match against Madrid was scheduled for 7 August. Thanks to goals from [[Raheem Sterling]] and [[Gabriel Jesus]], the Citizens once again defeated Madrid 2–1, achieving a 4–2 victory on aggregate and advancing to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-v-real-madrid-ucl-2nd-leg-match-report-63732423|title=City head to Lisbon after deserved win over Real Madrid|website=mancity.com|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|date=7 August 2020|access-date=23 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/champions-league-lyon-63732430|title=City to play Lyon in Champions League quarter-final |website=mancity.com |publisher=Manchester City F.C.|date=7 August 2020|access-date=23 August 2020}}</ref> However, Manchester City once again exited the competition at the next stage, losing 1–3 to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on 15 August in a one-off game held at the neutral [[Estádio José Alvalade]] in Lisbon.

In the [[2019-20 Premier League|Premier League]], City were unable to maintain their consistency from the previous two seasons. Key players [[Aymeric Laporte]] and [[Leroy Sané]] endured extended injury layoffs from the beginning of the season until early 2020. Laporte's absence in particular impacted the team's defensive capabilities and their effectiveness against opposition set up to quickly counterattack on the break. City already dropped more league points (19) by the end of December 2019 than they had in their entire previous two seasons.

For the second year in a row, City were the first top European team to reach 100 goals scored in all competitions when they beat [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] 4–0 in an [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]] fourth-round match on 26 January 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/51240666|title=Highlights: Manchester City 4-0 Fulham|work=BBC Sport|access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref>

On 14 February 2020, UEFA stated its intention to ban Manchester City from the all [[UEFA club competitions]] for the 2020–21 and 2021–22 seasons for alleged breaches of the [[UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations]].<ref name="UEFA statement1">{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/insideuefa/about-uefa/news/newsid=2638659.html |title=Club Financial Control Body Adjudicatory Chamber decision on Manchester City Football Club |website=UEFA.com |publisher=[[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]] |date=14 February 2020 |access-date=14 February 2020}}</ref> UEFA noted the club's right to appeal at the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS), and Manchester City then submitted an appeal on 26 February 2020.<ref name="CAS statement1">{{cite news |url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_6785_.pdf |title=The Court of Arbitration For Sport (CAS) Has Registered the Appeal of Manchester City v. UEFA |website=[[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] |access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref> As part of the appeal registration, the Court of Arbitration for Sport stated a date for the final decision would be in the first half of July 2020. The appeal was heard on 8 June 2020<ref name="CAS appeal">{{cite web|first=Gabriele|last=Marcotti|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/blog-marcottis-musings/story/4106533/man-citys-appeal-of-uefa-ban-whats-at-stake-for-city-and-financial-fair-play|title=Man City's appeal of UEFA ban: What's at stake for City and Financial Fair Play|website=ESPN.com|date=5 June 2020}}</ref> and upheld on 13 July, with the ban overturned.<ref>{{cite web |title= Decision in the arbitration procedure between Manchester City FC & UEFA |url= https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_6785_Decision.pdf |website=The Court of Arbitration for Sport|access-date=13 July 2020}}</ref>

On 1 March 2020, City won their third [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in a row and their fourth in five seasons, defeating [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] 2–1 at Wembley Stadium in the [[2020 EFL Cup final|final]].

In March, the season became affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/51859553|title=Coronavirus: UK government considering banning sporting fixtures|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020}}</ref> On 10 March, the match between Manchester City and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], due to be played the next day, was postponed after a number of Arsenal players made close contact with Olympiacos owner [[Evangelos Marinakis]], who had tested positive for infection with the [[SARS-CoV-2|coronavirus]], when the two teams had met in the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] 13 days earlier.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester City vs. Arsenal postponed after players exposed to Olympiakos owner Evangelos Marinakis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-premier-league/story/4071980/arsenal-vs-manchester-city-postponed-after-players-exposed-to-olympiakos-owner-evangelos-marinakis |website=ESPN |access-date=10 March 2020 }}</ref> On 12 March, it was revealed that three Leicester City players were self-isolating.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51856906|title=Coronavirus: Three Leicester City players in isolation after showing symptoms|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Manchester City also announced that their defender [[Benjamin Mendy]] was also self-isolating, after a family member displayed symptoms of the virus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51864868|title=Benjamin Mendy: Man City player self-isolating, family member in hospital|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Later in the evening, it was confirmed that Arsenal head coach [[Mikel Arteta]] had tested positive for coronavirus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51865442|title=Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager tests positive for coronavirus|work=BBC Sport|date=13 March 2020}}</ref> On 13 March, following an emergency meeting between the Premier League, [[The Football Association]] (FA), the [[English Football League]] and the [[FA Women's Super League]], it was unanimously decided to suspend professional football in England until at least 4 April 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1645173|title=Premier League, FA, EFL and WSL unite to postpone fixtures|date=13 March 2020|work=Premier League|access-date=13 March 2020}}</ref> On 19 March, the suspension was extended to at least 30 April 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51962751|title=Coronavirus: English football suspension extended until at least 30 April|work=BBC Sport|date=19 March 2020}}</ref> At the same time, the FA agreed to extend the season indefinitely, past the scheduled end date of 1 June.

In late May 2020, the [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK Government]] began to ease the lockdown measures, which had been taken to combat the COVID-19 contagion, and it was duly announced on 28 May that the Premier League clubs had agreed to play the remaining 92 Premier League and FA Cup fixtures in empty stadiums and with modified rules to minimise contagion from 17 June 2020 onward. City restarted the season with a postponed game in hand against Arsenal on 17 June, winning 3–0. On 25 June, City lost 2–1 away to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], and as a result Liverpool were confirmed as 2019–20 Premier League champions with seven rounds of games to be played. A week later, on 2 July, City were able to assuage some of the disappointment of losing the Premier League title to their [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester City F.C. rivalry|rivals]] when they beat Liverpool 4–0 in a home league match, with a fifth goal in stoppage time disallowed by the [[Video assistant referee|VAR]], also avenging November's controversial 1–3 loss.

In beating [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] 5–0 on 8 July, City achieved a pass completion rate of 93.7% – the highest accuracy on record in the Premier League since 2003–04 (when detailed passing statistics were first measured). [[Riyad Mahrez]] reaching 10 Premier League goals in the season in the same game also ensured City would be the first English top-flight side to have five different players score at least 10 league goals in a single season since [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in [[1984–85 Everton F.C. season|1984–85]] (Sterling, De Bruyne, Agüero, Jesus, Mahrez).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hafez |first1=Shamoon |title=City vs. Newcastle match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53283254 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=9 July 2020}}</ref> The 5–0 away victory against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on 11 July then confirmed that City would finish the season as runners-up to Liverpool in the league. The Blues scored 102 league goals in 2019–20; it was the fifth time they reached a century of goals after [[1936–37 Manchester City F.C. season|1936–37]], [[1957–58 Manchester City F.C. season|1957–58]], [[2013–14 Manchester City F.C. season|2013–14]] and [[2017–18 Manchester City F.C. season|2017–18]], an English record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/printoutfiles/competitions/uefachampionsleague/2020/e/e_2030144_pk.pdf|title=UEFA Champions League - 2019/20 Season Match Press Kits|website=UEFA|date=21 December 2020}}</ref>

In the restarted FA Cup, City defeated Newcastle 2–0 away from home on 28 June, advancing to the semi-finals where they faced Arsenal at Wembley. However, inform [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|Aubameyang]] scored a brace and lukewarm City were shut out, being denied an opportunity to defend their title in a showcase [[2020 FA Cup final|final]]. The Gunners went on to win a record 14th FA Cup title in the final, defeating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].

The end of the 2019–20 season marked the end of [[David Silva]]'s ten-year stint with the club. Silva's final appearance in the Champions League quarter-final defeat to Lyon was his 436th for City; in doing so he entered the top 10 all-time [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Appearances|appearance makers]] for the club, as well as becoming the first modern-era player to reach this level in 34 years. Silva also ended his career at City as the club's most decorated player at the time, with fourteen league and cup winner medals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Edwards |first1=John |title=David Silva A Glittering Decade of Success |url=https://www.mancity.com/features/davidsilvadecadeofsuccess/ |website=mancity.com |access-date=24 August 2020}}</ref> Due to COVID-19 precautions, Silva's final appearances had to be played behind closed doors. City hoped there would be an opportunity in the following season for fans to return in order to give him a proper sendoff.

[[Kevin De Bruyne]] was recognised in the end of season awards for his performances at City, being named the [[Premier League Player of the Season]] and [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]], despite Liverpool winning the Premier League title that year. De Bruyne had already won the club's own Player of the Season Award for the third time in five years, and the Premier League's [[Premier League Playmaker of the Season|Playmaker of the Season]] award for providing a league-leading 20 assists, equalling the record of most assists in a Premier League season set by [[Thierry Henry]] in [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Leigh |first1=Neil |title=De Bruyne Named Premier League Player of the Season |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/kevin-de-bruyne-premier-league-player-of-the-season-63733021 |website=mancity.com |access-date=24 August 2020}}</ref>

===FA Community Shield===
{{main|2019 FA Community Shield}}
Due to winning both the [[2018–19 Premier League]] and [[2018–19 FA Cup]], Manchester City faced Premier League runners-up [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the FA Community Shield.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/fa-cup/544710/when-is-the-community-shield-liverpool-manchester-city/|title=When is the Community Shield? Date confirmed as Liverpool's season starts early despite title heartache|date=7 June 2019|website=talkSPORT|language=en-US|access-date=1 July 2019}}</ref> Manchester City were the [[2018 FA Community Shield|defending champions]] and successfully defended their title.

===FA Cup===
{{main|2019–20 FA Cup}}
Manchester City entered the FA Cup in the third round as [[2018–19 FA Cup|defending champions]]. The third-round draw was made on 2 December 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50637970 |title =FA Cup third round: Liverpool draw Everton in third round
|date=2 December 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=2 December 2019}}</ref> The fourth-round draw was made by [[Alex Scott (footballer, born 1984)|Alex Scott]] and [[David O'Leary]] on Monday, 6 January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Emirates FA Cup Fourth Round Draw is Complete |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2020/jan/06/fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-060120  |publisher=[[The Football Association]] |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref> The draw for the fifth round was made on 27 January 2020, live on ''[[The One Show]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup fifth-round draw: Wayne Rooney could face former side Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51271468 |access-date=28 January 2020 |work=[[BBC]]}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2019–20 EFL Cup}}
Manchester City entered the EFL Cup in the third round as [[2018–19 EFL Cup|defending champions]]. The third-round draw was confirmed on 28 August 2019, live on [[Sky Sports]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup Round Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2019/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw-to-take-place-live-on-sky-sports/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |access-date=30 August 2019}}</ref> The draw for the fourth round was made on 25 September 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup Round Four draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2019/september/carabao-cup-round-four-draw-confirmed/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref> The quarter-finals draw was conducted on 31 October, live on [[BBC Radio 2]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City to play at Oxford in EFL Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50246769 |publisher=[[BBC]] |access-date=31 October 2019}}</ref>

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2019–20 UEFA Champions League}}

====Group stage====
{{main|2019–20 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group C}}
Manchester City entered the competition in the group stage as the reigning Premier League champions. They were drawn in Group C with [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]], [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] and [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]].<ref>{{cite web |title=UEFA Champions League group stage draw |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/draws/2020/2001140/ |publisher=UEFA |access-date=29 August 2019}}</ref>
